prompt: The golden rule of French endings: final s, t, d, x are usually…
options: silent — you write them but never say them
explain: très, veux, quand, pas — the last letter is for your EYES, not your mouth. This is why dictation feels hard: you must write letters you can't hear.

hint: /ʒə vø/ — the x is silent but must be written.
explain: je veux — silent x. (Not Vuex — that's your day job leaking in.)

hint: Same sound /vø/, but il takes t.
explain: je veuX, tu veuX, il veuT — sound identical, endings differ.
quand /kɑ̃/ — the d only exists on paper.

prompt: Spell: not (the second half of ne…)
explain: pas — one of thousands of silent final s.

hint: /tʁɛ/ — accent grave on e, silent s.
The -es is completely silent — sounds exactly like je parle.
explain: tu parles — je parle / tu parles / il parle all sound the same; only spelling changes.

prompt: Why do je parle / tu parles / il parle all sound identical?
explain: Your ear already knows these verbs. Dictation is teaching your fingers the silent endings.
